newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy state accounts could be balanced - BOI's Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy state accounts could be balanced - BOI's Fazio.

text.p: Italy's public accounts could be brought back into balance over the next decade and the ratio of public debt to gross domestic product lowered if the economy grew faster, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said.

"In the context of faster growth, the elimination of the deficit on current spending by 1999 and the lowering of the ratio between public and gross domestic product to below 100 percent by the middle of the next decade are possible," he said.
Fazio was speaking at the annual assembly of the Bank of Italy.

The economy could return to a growth rate of three percent a year but the outlook was for unsatisfactory growth over the next three years while the government wrestled to contain the public deficit, said Fazio.

The government's three-year economic strategy, approved by the cabinet on Friday, aims to lower the debt to GDP ratio from 121.11 percent in 1998 to 116.35 percent by the year 2000. Rome newsroom +396-6782560
